morphology_interfaces.base: two trees as patients, agent unknown
morphology_interfaces.affix: nominative dual agreement and instrumental query

nominal_positions.interpretation: The quality of the speaker. Its u-stem has the nominative ending here.
Attribute of Mārīca, the addressee of jagāda. Its a-stem supplies am.
The epic’s one attributed fault is among the excluded causes.
The two trees have fallen and agree with the past passive participle. Kena asks after the agent.
The day and night pair makes different forms. The verb is transitive dual and the commentary supplies rūpāṇi.

source_policy_decisions.decision: Keep both initial c consonants, with their attributed explanations, and both final stem vowels. Each verse adjective applies to a different person.
Separation belongs to the input base. Supplying another semantic negation at the suffix changes the interpretation. Preserve both external sandhis in the Upaniṣad.
Primary independent evidence for the first-syllable pitch at 3.55.11. The longer word and the compound at 9.112 have their own textual identity.
The epic’s four parallel exclusion phrases license accusatives. In the Gītā a separated instrumental depends on vinā. The grammatical case belongs to its dependent.

The literary locator is established. Retain plural elephant-caused faults in the Kāśikā and singular in the named epic edition. Repeated wind, rain and the shared syntactic rule retain earlier ownership.
